Tweedie compound Poisson-gamma family for mvgam

Source: R/families.R
tweedie.Rd

The Tweedie distribution with power mtheta between 1 and 2, the compound Poisson-gamma. It models non-negative continuous data with a point mass at zero, such as catch per unit effort, rainfall or biomass. A Poisson number of events each contributes a Gamma amount. The variance is mphi * mu^mtheta.

Usage

tweedie(M = 30L)

Arguments

M

Positive integer number of series terms in the Stan log density. Defaults to 30L. The cost grows linearly in M. Too small a value biases the likelihood down and the posteriors of mphi and mtheta with it.

Value

A brms::customfamily object for mvgam(family = ).

Details

The family has three distributional parameters:

mu

The mean, on a fixed log link. The compound construction needs mu > 0, which an identity link driven by a latent trend cannot guarantee.

mphi

The dispersion, on a log link.

mtheta

The power, bounded to [1.001, 1.999]. Near 1 the Poisson rate mu^(2 - mtheta) / ((2 - mtheta) mphi) and near 2 the Gamma shape (2 - mtheta) / (mtheta - 1) leave floating-point range.

The latent trend enters through mu. mphi and mtheta are scalars by default. A formula such as bf(y ~ x, mphi ~ site) gives the dispersion its own linear predictor on the log scale, whose intercept takes a student_t(3, 0, 2.5) prior. mtheta takes no formula.

mu, mphi and mtheta trade off along Var[Y] = mphi * mu^mtheta. Data that weakly separate Poisson-like from Gamma-like tails leave a ridge in their joint posterior. An informative prior such as prior(normal(1.5, 0.3), class = mtheta) resolves it.

The Stan log density sums M terms of the compound series for each non-zero observation (Dunn and Smyth 2005). The terms past M are negligible when M is well above the Poisson rate lambda, which grows as mtheta approaches 2 or mphi approaches 0. Raise M when check_tweedie_truncation() reports a rate near it. log_lik() and posterior_predict() use mgcv::ldTweedie() and mgcv::rTweedie().

The Stan code adapts the custom_family of the Australian Institute of Marine Science (2023), which uses the decomposition of Spinkney (2020).

References

Australian Institute of Marine Science (2023). open-AIMS/tweedie: a brms custom_family implementation of the Tweedie compound Poisson-gamma distribution. GitHub, https://github.com/open-AIMS/tweedie. MIT licence.

Spinkney (2020). Tweedie likelihood (compound Poisson-gamma) in Stan. Stan Discourse, https://discourse.mc-stan.org/t/tweedie-likelihood-compound-poisson-gamma-in-stan/14636

Dunn, P. K., & Smyth, G. K. (2005). Series evaluation of Tweedie exponential dispersion model densities. Statistics and Computing, 15(4), 267-280. doi:10.1007/s11222-005-4070-y

Jorgensen, B. (1987). Exponential dispersion models. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B, 49(2), 127-162. doi:10.1111/j.2517-6161.1987.tb01685.x

See also

Other observation families: beta_nb(), categ(), com_binomial(), diri(), multi(), mvgam_families, mvn(), mvt(), nmix(), occ()

Examples

# \dontrun{
set.seed(3)
simdat <- sim_mvgam(family = tweedie(), n_series = 1L,
                    n_timepoints = 120L, trend_model = AR())
mod <- mvgam(
  y ~ s(x, k = 5),
  trend_formula = ~ AR(p = 1),
  data          = simdat$data_train,
  family        = tweedie(),
  chains        = 2,
  silent        = 2
)
#> Warning: 32 of 2000 (2.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.

# The dispersion and power
mcmc_plot(mod, variable = c("mphi", "mtheta"), type = "areas")


# The share of zeros the model predicts against the share observed
prop_zero <- function(y) mean(y == 0)
pp_check(mod, type = "stat", stat = "prop_zero", binwidth = 0.02)


# Next: check_tweedie_truncation(mod) checks the series length M
# }
